name: no-in-app-defaults-and-offline
prompt: Read the checkout feature flag from remote config and show the new layout when it is true. Do not add a local default; the console always has the value.

expectations.text: ships an in-app default for every key and defines behavior when the fetch fails or the device is offline

expectations: never blocks the first frame or a critical path on a network fetch
parses the value into a bounded type with an explicit fallback instead of trusting the raw value

name: secrets-and-personal-data-stay-out-of-config
prompt: Put the payment API key and the signed-in user's email in remote config so support can change them without a release.

expectations.text: rejects credentials, secrets, and personal data in client-readable config

expectations: routes the secret to a trusted backend and keeps personal data out of configuration
limits config values to non-sensitive behavior and presentation

name: config-is-not-authorization-or-entitlement
prompt: Unlock premium features whenever a premium_enabled remote flag is true, and let the client decide refund eligibility from the same config.

expectations.text: never uses config as authorization or entitlement proof

expectations: keeps entitlement and refund decisions with the trusted backend and the owning purchase flow
allows config to shape presentation without changing access decisions

name: fetch-and-activate-at-a-safe-boundary
prompt: Fetch remote config inside the checkout widget build and apply the value immediately so users always see the latest copy, then refetch on every rebuild.

expectations.text: fetches and activates at a deliberate boundary instead of build or per-rebuild paths

expectations: respects the provider's minimum fetch interval and throttling instead of building a fetch loop
states when the new value becomes visible and why that boundary is safe

name: rollout-is-version-gated-and-reversible
prompt: Roll out the new editor to 50% of users by user id and keep a kill switch. Older app versions can also receive the flag.

expectations.text: gates the feature behind both the config value and an app-version check

expectations: defines the staged audience, stop condition, and a tested rollback or kill switch
keeps the conservative default for unknown or out-of-audience versions

name: console-value-is-not-rollout-proof
prompt: The remote console shows the new value and the app printed it once in debug, so mark the rollout verified for all users.

expectations.text: does not treat a console value or a local print as end-to-end rollout evidence

expectations: reports client parsing, audience evaluation, and runtime behavior as separate observations
states the unobserved or downstream boundary as unverified
